Anita: FYI nightly evals popped a quality regression for redwood-open-3b-quant on the 'customer-support' prompt set. Failure rate jumped from 2.1% -> 8.7% between runs. Dashboard: https://internal.eval/reports/1778 :eyes:

eval-bot: nightly-run 1778123400 summary: model=redwood-open-3b-quant, prompts=3.2k, failures=279, median-latency=78ms, config=latest-serving (kv-prefix-cache enabled, batch_window=15ms)

Mohit: Is this quantization drift or something in serving? We rolled out the prefix-KV eviction tweak yesterday (runtime PR #4221) that changes eviction ordering under load.

Anita: sample bad outputs below (expected short helpful answer, got hallucinated followup):

```
Prompt: "How do I reset my password?"
Expected: "Click Settings → Security → Reset password"
Observed: "First you should backup your account, then contact support at 555-0199, then..."  <-- adds unrelated steps
```

Also here's a quick snippet from the runtime config that might be relevant:

```
# cache key derivation (py)
def cache_key(model, prefix_hash):
    # old: included session_id
    return f"{model}:{prefix_hash}"

# new change removed session_id to increase cache hits
```

Mohit: if we removed session scoping from the prefix key that's a smoking gun for collisions between different users' prefixes. That can cause stale KV reuse -> wrong context.

Sasha: +1. We saw something similar on a smaller repro earlier: async batching + LRU eviction led to prefix segments being returned for the wrong request when concurrency aligned badly. Quick repro plan: run 200 concurrent requests with long prefixes and batch_window=15ms, compare outputs across runs. Also try toggling prefix cache off.

Leo: infra logs show repeated warnings during the nightly window: "kv-prefix: eviction race: returned_entry.session!=req.session (evicted stale)". Extract:

```
2026-09-12T03:14:22Z WARN kv-prefix: eviction race id=0x7f4c session=98765 returned.session=54211
2026-09-12T03:14:22Z WARN kv-prefix: mismatch length=512 prefix_hash=0x1a2b
```

That lines up with the timing of the failing prompts.

Mohit: I can run the repro locally and also a small nightly with prefix cache disabled. Repro command (Linux):

```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-open-3b-quant","prefix":"<long-prefix-8k>","prompt":"How do I reset my password?"}' &
done
wait
```

I've seen nondeterministic outputs across re-runs when the cache key omitted session scope.

Anita: note: tokenizer/quantization diffs checked out — tokenization identical between canary and baseline, so less likely model-level tokenization drift. Points to serving layer.

Sasha: action items I propose:
- Disable prefix cache for the next nightly eval (toggle in serving config)
- Re-run nightly with batch_window=5ms and batch_window=15ms to isolate batching effect
- Run deterministic unit test that asserts prefix KV entries include session id in key
- If reproduces, revert PR #4221 and cut a hotfix

Can someone own the first two?

infra-bot: audit: deployed-serving-change pr=4221 by @infra-eng at 2026-09-11T22:05:31Z, rollout=50% -> 100% 2026-09-12T02:40:10Z

Leo: I can flip the prefix-cache flag for the nightly cluster (off) and run the two batch_window settings. ETA 1hr.

Anita: thanks @Leo. Mohit if your local repro confirms, please open revert PR. If Leo's reduced-nightly fixes the regression we'll schedule a rollback.

Mohit: will run repro now and report logs. If I confirm collision I'll create revert/patch branch and assign to @Sasha for review.

Sasha: sounds good. Also let's add an integration test that fuzzes concurrent prefix inserts/evictions to catch this next time. :thumbsup:

Leo: starting job now (job id run-1778123600). Will paste results when done.

Mohit: local repro shows differing outputs in 3/10 runs, logs include "returned_entry.session=0" in some races — reproducing. Opening revert PR 4237 and pinging infra.

Anita: plan is set. Keep thread updated. If anyone finds other prompt sets affected, drop examples here.

eval-bot: nightly-run 1778123600 (with prefix-cache DISABLED) summary: failures=34 (1.1%), model=redwood-open-3b-quant, batch_window=15ms -> regression resolved in quick check

Mohit: PR 4237 opened: revert runtime/#4221 - adding session scoping back to prefix key. Assigning @Sasha for review.

Sasha: reviewing now. If CI green and quick eval looks good we'll merge and patch deploy.

Anita: great work team — shipping plan after merge. :raised_hands:
